info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package knowledge is your team's wiki and your agents' memory, searchable by meaning.

get.summary: Returns every supported knowledge connector with THIS org's connection state and the REAL number of documents each has ingested into the org's store.
get.description:
Returns every supported knowledge connector with THIS org's
connection state and the REAL number of documents each has ingested into the
org's store. A provider that is configured for the deployment but not yet
connected appears as disconnected, so the console can offer a Connect button.
No secret is ever returned.

get.summary: Returns the ONE catalog of everything a caller can connect: every first-party connector and every long-tail one, in a single list sorted by provider.
get.description:
Returns the ONE catalog of everything a caller can
connect: every first-party connector and every long-tail one, in a single list
sorted by provider. `configured` reports whether this deployment holds OAuth
credentials for a source, so the console can show Connect rather than a dead
button, and `kind` is a badge only — the connect and sync lifecycle is
identical for both. The catalog itself is org-independent; a validated
principal is still required. It is metadata only: no secret is ever returned.

delete.summary: Revokes a connection: it tombstones the stored credential so a later sync cannot reuse it, removes this provider's passages from the org's store, and marks the connector disconnected.
delete.description:
Revokes a connection: it tombstones the stored credential
so a later sync cannot reuse it, removes this provider's passages from the
org's store, and marks the connector disconnected. The documents already
ingested stay in the org's store — they are the org's own data — but stop being
retrievable by search; a caller deletes them through the document surface.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider is the connector to act on: github, slack, google or notion.

get.summary: CompleteConnectorOAuth finishes an OAuth connection: it exchanges the provider's code for a token, seals that token in KMS, and records the connection.
get.description:
CompleteConnectorOAuth finishes an OAuth connection: it exchanges the
provider's code for a token, seals that token in KMS, and records the
connection. THE ORG COMES FROM THE SIGNED STATE, not from a header and not from
the provider, so an attacker cannot bind their own account to someone else's
org — a tampered, expired or foreign-provider state is refused outright. The
token itself is never returned, never written into the document, and never
logged; the document holds only its KMS path.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider is the connector completing its flow, from the path.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Code is the provider's authorization code, exchanged for a token.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State is the org-bound value this server signed at connect time.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Error is the provider's denial reason when the user refused consent.

get.summary: StartConnectorOAuth returns the provider authorize URL the console opens to connect this org's account.
get.description:
StartConnectorOAuth returns the provider authorize URL the console opens to
connect this org's account. There is no server-side redirect — the console
stays in control of the navigation. The URL carries a state this server SIGNED
over the caller's validated org, so the connection the callback completes can
only ever land in that org.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider is the connector to act on: github, slack, google or notion.

post.summary: Pulls the provider's documents for the caller's org and files them as knowledge sources, which the store's own hook then indexes — so a synced document is retrievable exactly like a hand-written page.
post.description:
Pulls the provider's documents for the caller's org and files
them as knowledge sources, which the store's own hook then indexes — so a
synced document is retrievable exactly like a hand-written page. The org is the
validated tenant and the credential is read from KMS, so an org can only ever
sync its own connection. A provider failure is reported honestly (502) and
recorded on the connector rather than silently swallowed.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Provider is the connector to act on: github, slack, google or notion.

get.summary: Answers the caller's org files, most recently changed first, each with its status and stage — optionally only those in one bucket, which is how Drive shows a folder's files with their index state.
get.description:
Answers the caller's org files, most recently changed first, each
with its status and stage — optionally only those in one bucket, which is how
Drive shows a folder's files with their index state.

post.summary: Makes an object in one of the caller's org buckets a workspace file.
post.description:
Makes an object in one of the caller's org buckets a workspace
file. Upload the bytes first — POST /v1/s3/buckets/{bucket}/objects mints a
presigned PUT, POST /v1/s3/buckets/{bucket}/uploads starts a multipart upload
for a large one — then register the key here. The object's name, type and
size are read from the store. The file is recorded as queued, a file_stored
event is stated on the org's event plane, and a durable ingest is queued that
extracts its text and structure, summarizes its table of contents, cuts and
embeds its passages and links it into the org's graph. An archive (.zip) is
unpacked and every file inside becomes a workspace file of its own. Poll GET
/v1/knowledge/files/{id} for status. Registering an object again answers the
same file, and re-indexes it only when the object changed or its last ingest
failed.

Registering a changed object again changes its file, which only the person
who registered it or an admin of the org may do: anyone else is refused 403
and the file keeps its version. Registering an unchanged object is a read.

post.summary: Grounds an answer in the caller's org files, table of contents first: candidate documents are found by searching their passages; a model reads their tables of contents — titles and one-line summaries — and picks the sections the answer is in; hybrid search drills into the passages of those sections; and the graph expands to the sections they link to or name the same entities as, in any file of the workspace.
post.description:
Grounds an answer in the caller's org files, table of contents
first: candidate documents are found by searching their passages; a model
reads their tables of contents — titles and one-line summaries — and picks
the sections the answer is in; hybrid search drills into the passages of
those sections; and the graph expands to the sections they link to or name
the same entities as, in any file of the workspace. Every passage cites its
file › section › paragraph, so an answer can say exactly where it came from.
This is what a chat runs before it answers about an attached file, and what
an agent runs before it answers about a workspace.

example.query: how long are backups retained, and who audits that?

post.summary: Answers the passages of the caller's org files that match a query, each citing its file › section › paragraph: the search behind Drive's box, and the first step an agent takes across a workspace.
post.description:
Answers the passages of the caller's org files that match a query,
each citing its file › section › paragraph: the search behind Drive's box,
and the first step an agent takes across a workspace. Name file ids to search
only those files; name none to search them all. A semantic leg compares the
query with every embedded passage and a full-text leg finds the passages
holding its words; the two are fused, so a passage both found comes first.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller's org files from the index — its table of contents, passages, full-text rows, mentions and links — and its record.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller's org files from the index — its table of
contents, passages, full-text rows, mentions and links — and its record. The
file is gone from every read when this answers: its listing, its contents,
search and retrieval. What the index held of it is removed after, a batch at
a time, so forgetting a file of any size answers at once. The object itself
stays in its bucket; delete it there. Drive calls this when it deletes a file.

Only the person who registered the file or an admin of the org may forget it;
anyone else in the org, who can still read it, is refused 403. A file
registered before uploaders were recorded is forgotten by an admin alone.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the file's id, as POST /v1/knowledge/files answered it.

get.summary: Answers one of the caller's org files: what it is, where its bytes are, and how far its ingest has got.
get.description:
Answers one of the caller's org files: what it is, where its bytes
are, and how far its ingest has got. 404 for an id the org holds no file for.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the file's id, as POST /v1/knowledge/files answered it.

get.summary: Answers one of the caller's org files' place in the org's graph: the files it links to and is linked from (a hyperlink, a citation by name), the files that name the same entities, and the entities it names.
get.description:
Answers one of the caller's org files' place in the org's graph:
the files it links to and is linked from (a hyperlink, a citation by name),
the files that name the same entities, and the entities it names. It is how
an agent finds the other documents a question about this one needs.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the file's id, as POST /v1/knowledge/files answered it.

get.summary: Answers one section of one of the caller's org files: its own text, its subsections, the sections it links to or shares entities with — in this file or another — and the entities it names.
get.description:
Answers one section of one of the caller's org files: its own
text, its subsections, the sections it links to or shares entities with —
in this file or another — and the entities it names. Open the document
itself with section 0.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: Section is the section's number in the file's table of contents.

get.summary: Answers one of the caller's org files' table of contents: every section in document order with its depth, its parent and a one-line summary.
get.description:
Answers one of the caller's org files' table of contents: every
section in document order with its depth, its parent and a one-line summary.
It is the map a reader — a person in Drive, or an agent deciding where to
look — reads before opening a section with GET
/v1/knowledge/files/{id}/sections/{section}.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the file's id, as POST /v1/knowledge/files answered it.

get.summary: Returns the caller org's knowledge as a node/edge graph shaped for a force-directed renderer: pages, memories and synced sources as nodes; the page parent tree, the wikilinks between pages, and each source's connector provenance as edges.
get.description:
Returns the caller org's knowledge as a node/edge graph
shaped for a force-directed renderer: pages, memories and synced sources as
nodes; the page parent tree, the wikilinks between pages, and each source's
connector provenance as edges. Wikilink targets are resolved HERE by title or
slug, so a rename never needs an edge rewrite and a link that matches no page
renders as its own "unresolved" node instead of vanishing. ?project= narrows
it. A store outage degrades to an honest empty graph, never a 5xx.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project narrows the graph to one project scope. Empty reads the whole org.

post.summary: Import an Obsidian, Notion, Roam or Evernote export into the org's knowledge base
post.description:
Ingests an uploaded export as a tree of kb.page documents with its link structure intact. `?format=` picks the normalizer — obsidian, notion, roam or evernote — and the export arrives as a multipart `file` part, or as the raw request body when there is no multipart part: an Obsidian or Notion vault zip, a Roam JSON (raw or inside the zip Roam downloads), or an Evernote .enex.

The pages are filed through the SAME ingest path a connector sync uses, so the kb.page hook indexes each one for retrieval AND extracts its `[[wikilinks]]` into kb.link edges — the imported vault is searchable and its graph is navigable without a second pass. Parents are filed before their children, and each page takes a slug unique within the org (suffixed -2, -3, … on collision), so a re-import adds pages rather than overwriting the ones already there.

Scoped to the caller's validated org; `?project=` narrows every imported page to one project. No validated principal is 403, and an org that has not installed the kb module is refused with the install call to make first. The bounds are 64 MB per upload, 5000 pages and 8 MB per archive entry: pages past the five-thousandth are dropped and a larger entry is truncated at its bound, and a page the store rejects is skipped — so the answer's `imported` count is what was actually filed, not what was sent.

post.summary: Rebuilds the caller org's retrieval from its documents: every passage is removed, and every page, memory and source is cut into passages and embedded again with the configured model; the lexical index is reconciled to the same documents.
post.description:
Rebuilds the caller org's retrieval from its documents: every passage
is removed, and every page, memory and source is cut into passages and
embedded again with the configured model; the lexical index is reconciled to
the same documents. It is what an operator runs after the embedding model
changes — passages of another model are never compared with the query, so
until then they are unread — and what puts an org's retrieval right after an
outage of the ai plane. It requires ORG ADMIN and runs inline: an org's
knowledge is a few thousand documents, and the answer is the count.

The request has no body. Response: {"vectors": 412, "lexical": 412, "removed": 3, "failed": 0}

post.summary: Runs a hybrid search over the caller org's own knowledge — its wiki pages, its agent memories and everything its connectors have synced.
post.description:
Runs a hybrid search over the caller org's own knowledge —
its wiki pages, its agent memories and everything its connectors have synced.
This is the RAG entry point: an agent asks "what does this org know about X"
and the org's OWN knowledge answers. Two legs run and are fused by reciprocal
rank: a semantic leg that embeds the query and compares it with every passage
of every document in reach (a document is cut into passages of about 2000
bytes, so a fact deep in a long page is found), and a keyword leg over the
org's knowledge index. The org comes from the validated principal and its
passages live in its own database, so cross-tenant retrieval is impossible. A
failed leg answers 200 with what the other leg found and degraded=true, never
a 5xx.

example.query: how do we rotate the signing key

bucket.description:
Bucket is the org bucket the object is in, by the friendly name
/v1/s3/buckets lists.

chars.description: Chars is the length of the text read out of the file, in bytes.

clipped.description:
Clipped is true when only the file's beginning is indexed: its text ran
past the org's bound or the room the index has. Note says how far.

created.description: Created is when the file was first registered, in unix seconds.

done.description:
Done is how far the running stage has come, of Total: bytes of the file
read (extract), sections summarized (toc), cut into passages (passages)
and linked (graph), passages embedded (embed). Absent between stages and
once the ingest is done.

embedded.description:
Embedded is how many of those passages carry a vector — Passages once the
embed stage is done, unless Note says the file is embedded in part.

error.description:
Error is why a stored or failed file was not indexed — or, on a ready
file, why it is searched by its words alone — in words a person can act
on. Absent otherwise.

id.description:
ID names the file in its org. It is derived from the bucket and key, so
registering the same object twice answers the same file.

key.description:
Key is the object's key in that bucket. GET
/v1/s3/buckets/{bucket}/objects/{key} answers a signed download URL for it.

name.description: Name is the object's file name, the last segment of its key.

note.description:
Note says in words where the file is indexed less than whole and why: its
text past the org's bound or the room the index has, its passages past
the bound on vectors. Absent when the whole file is indexed every way.

parent.description:
Parent is the id of the archive this file was unpacked from. Absent for a
file uploaded on its own.

passages.description: Passages is how many passages its text was cut into.

project.description:
Project is the project scope it is indexed under. Absent for the org's
own files.

sections.description:
Sections is how many nodes its table of contents has, the document's own
root included.

size.description: Size is the object's length in bytes, as the store reports it.

stage.description:
Stage is the ingest stage the file is in: extract, toc, passages or graph
while indexing, embed while a ready file's vectors are written. Absent once
the ingest is done.

status.description:
Status is queued, indexing, ready, stored (kept but not indexed — Error
says why) or failed. A ready file's contents, passages and links are all
readable and its full text is searched; its vectors may still be filling
in (Stage embed), which adds search by meaning as it goes.

total.description: Total is what the running stage has to do in all, in Done's units.

type.description:
Type is the object's media type as the store holds it, or the one its
name implies when the store holds only the generic default.

updated.description: Updated is when its record last changed, in unix seconds.

configured.description:
Configured is whether THIS DEPLOYMENT holds the OAuth client credentials for
the provider. False means Connect would dead-end, so the console can offer it
disabled instead of broken. It is deployment-wide and says nothing about
whether the caller's org has connected the source — that is the connector
list's `status`.

description.description:
Description is one line of shop copy: what connecting this source pulls in.
Native connectors carry written prose; a provider-backed one reads
"activepieces connector (<provider>)".

displayName.description:
DisplayName is the label to show a person. First-party connectors carry a
written name ("GitHub", "Google Drive"); a provider-backed one falls back to the
provider capitalized, because the rich activepieces metadata lives behind a
cross-service call this read will not make.

provider.description:
Provider is the source's id and the address every connector op takes it by
(/v1/knowledge/connectors/:provider). One of github, slack, google, notion.

connectors.description: Connectors is every connectable source, sorted by provider.

cite.description: Cite is how an answer cites it: file › section path › ¶part.

file.description: File is the file the passage is from.

part.description: Part is the passage's place in its section, from 1.

score.description: Score is the fused rank score, comparable within one response only.

section.description: Section is the section it is in.

text.description:
Text is the passage: a span of its section of about 2000 bytes, never
crossing into another section.

via.description:
Via is how retrieval reached it: search (it matched), toc (it is in a
section the table of contents pointed at) or graph (a linked section).

why.description: Why says, for a passage reached through the graph, which edge led there.

account.description: Account names the connected external account, when the provider reports one.

provider.description: Provider is the connector this answer is about.

status.description: Status is the connection state: connected or disconnected.

account.description: Account names the connected external account. Absent until the org connects.

configured.description: Configured is true when this deployment holds OAuth credentials for the provider.

docCount.description: DocCount is the live count of this provider's documents in the org's store.

error.description: Error is the last sync failure, if any. Absent until the org connects.

kind.description: Kind is "native" for a first-party Go connector, "provider" for a long-tail one.

lastSync.description: LastSync is when the last pull finished. Absent until the org connects.

status.description: Status is connected, disconnected, syncing or error.

bucket.description:
Bucket and Key are where its bytes are: GET
/v1/s3/buckets/{bucket}/objects/{key} answers a signed download URL.

key.description: Key is the object's key in Bucket.

type.description: Type is the file's media type.

files.description: Files is how many other files of the org name it too.

kind.description: Kind is person, org, product, place or term.

name.description: Name is the entity as the text names it.

sections.description: Sections is how many of the file's sections name it.

entities.description: Entities are the entities it names, most mentioned first.

file.description: File is the file the graph is of.

links.description: Links are the other files it is joined to, strongest first.

bucket.description:
Bucket is one of the org's buckets, by the friendly name /v1/s3/buckets
lists. Required.

key.description: Key is the object's key in that bucket, as the upload wrote it. Required.

project.description: Project indexes the file under one project scope. Empty is the org's own.

direction.description:
Direction is out when this file links to the other, in when the other
links to this one, and shared when the two name the same entities.

file.description: File is the other file, by id.

kind.description:
Kind is href (a hyperlink), cites (the text names the file), xref (a
cross-reference inside one document) or entity (shared mentions).

label.description: Label is the link's own text, or the entities the two files share.

name.description: Name is the other file's name.

weight.description:
Weight is how many edges of this kind join the two; for shared entities,
how many entities they share.

files.description:
Files restricts the search to these file ids. Empty searches every file
the org holds.

limit.description: Limit bounds the passages returned. Default 8, maximum 50.

project.description: Project restricts the search to files indexed under one project scope.

query.description: Query is the question or phrase. Required.

degraded.description:
Degraded is true when a leg failed — the query could not be embedded, or
the full-text index could not be read — and Passages are what the other
leg found.

passages.description: Passages are the matching passages, best first, at most Limit.

files.description: Files are the org's files, most recently changed first.

id.description: ID is the file whose index was removed.

from.description:
From is the id of the node the edge starts at: the child page for a parent
edge, the page holding the wikilink for a link edge, the kb.source for a
provenance edge. Always one of Nodes.

to.description:
To is the id of the node the edge points at: the parent page, the linked
page, the kb.connector. Always one of Nodes — a wikilink matching no page
points at a synthetic "unresolved:<lowercased title>" node rather than
dangling.

name.description: the document name (empty for synthetic nodes)

project.description:
Project is the project scope the underlying document was saved under. Absent
for a document saved with none, and for the synthetic nodes — unresolved link
targets and connectors belong to no project. When ?project= narrows the
graph, every page, memory and source node carries that value.

degraded.description:
Degraded is true when the store was unreachable and this graph is honestly
empty rather than wrong. Absent on a normal answer.

edges.description: Edges are the parent tree, the resolved wikilinks and the connector provenance.

nodes.description: Nodes are the pages, memories, sources, connectors and unresolved link targets.

doctype.description:
DocType is which kind of knowledge matched, by address: kb.page (a wiki
page), kb.memory (a unit of agent memory) or kb.source (a document a
connector ingested).
Those three are the whole indexed set, and searchIn.DocTypes filters on them.

name.description:
Name is the document's name in the framework store — the id to read or open
it with. Unique per (org, doctype), so it identifies the document with
DocType and not alone.

project.description:
Project is the project scope the document was saved under. Absent for a
document saved with none, which is also why a project-scoped query cannot
reach it.

provider.description:
Provider is the connector that ingested the document — github, slack, google
or notion. Absent for a page or memory written in the product, which came
from no connector.

score.description:
Score is the cosine similarity between the query's embedding and the
document's BEST-matching passage, from -1 to 1, higher being closer. A
document is cut into passages of about 2000 bytes, each embedded on its own,
so a fact deep in a long page scores as high as one in its first paragraph.
0 for a document only the lexical leg found, which has no similarity to
report. There is no absolute cutoff: what counts as a good score moves with
the query and the embedding model, so compare scores within one response and
not across queries.

title.description:
Title is the document's title. Empty for a document saved without one; it
is a label to show, never the id (that is Name).

url.description:
URL is the document's link back into the app it was ingested from. Absent
when the document carries none, which is the normal case for pages and
memories.

authorizeUrl.description: AuthorizeURL is the provider's authorize endpoint with an org-bound signed state.

connectors.description: Connectors is every supported provider with this org's connection state.

ingested.description: Ingested is how many documents landed in the org's knowledge store.

provider.description: Provider is the connector that was pulled.

file.description: File is the file it is in.

failed.description:
Failed is how many documents could not be indexed; each is logged with its
name and has no passages — the rest of the rebuild went on without it.

lexical.description:
Lexical is how many rows the org's lexical index holds now; 0 in a
deployment without the index app.

removed.description:
Removed is how many rows the lexical index held for documents that no
longer exist; 0 without the index app.

vectors.description:
Vectors is how many documents were read back, cut into passages, embedded
and written to the org's passage store, which was emptied first — so it now
holds these documents' passages and nothing else.

files.description:
Files are the files the question is about — the files a chat message
references. Empty asks the whole workspace. The graph may still reach
files beyond them.

limit.description:
Limit bounds the passages drilled out of the chosen sections. Default 8,
maximum 24. The graph adds up to four more.

project.description: Project restricts retrieval to files indexed under one project scope.

query.description: Query is the question to answer. Required.

degraded.description: Degraded is true when a search leg failed along the way.

passages.description:
Passages are the passages drilled out of those sections, then those the
graph reached, each citing file › section › paragraph.

picked.description:
Picked says how the sections were chosen: whole when the documents were
short enough to read every section, model when a model read the tables of
contents, search when the sections of the best passages stood in — the
documents had no headings to choose by, or no model answered.

sections.description:
Sections are the sections chosen from the candidate documents' tables of
contents.

doctypes.description:
DocTypes restricts retrieval to a subset of the indexed knowledge doctypes
(kb.page, kb.memory, kb.source). An empty or foreign list reads all of them.

limit.description: Limit bounds the hits returned. Default 10, maximum 50.

project.description: Project narrows retrieval to one project scope.

query.description: Query is the natural-language question. Required.

degraded.description:
Degraded is true when a leg FAILED — the query could not be embedded, or a
store could not be read — and Hits are what the other leg found, possibly
nothing. A RAG caller continues with what it got instead of failing the turn.
Absent on a normal answer, including one from a deployment that runs only
one of the legs.

hits.description:
Hits are the matching documents, most relevant first: the order is the two
legs fused, so a document both the semantic and the keyword leg found comes
before one only a single leg found.

id.description:
ID is the section's number in its file's table of contents; 0 is the
document itself.

path.description:
Path is the section's place in its document: the titles from the
document's own down to it, joined by " › ".

file.description: File is the file the linked section is in.

kind.description:
Kind is href, xref, cites, or entity (the two sections name the same
entities).

label.description: Label is the link's text, or the entities the two share.

children.description: Children are its subsections, to open next.

entities.description: Entities are the entities it names.

file.description: File is the file it is in.

links.description: Links are the sections the graph reaches from it, strongest first.

text.description: Text is its own text — up to its first subsection — at most 64 KB.

id.description: ID is the section's number; 0 is the document itself.

level.description: Level is its depth: 0 for the document, 1 for a top-level heading.

parent.description: Parent is the id of the section it sits in; -1 for the document.

size.description: Size is how many bytes of the document it spans, subsections included.

summary.description: Summary is a one-line account of what it covers.

synthetic.description:
Synthetic is true for a section the index cut out of a long run of text
the document gave no structure to.

file.description: File is the file it is of.

sections.description:
Sections are its nodes in document order, the document first; Parent
makes them a tree.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
